newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Victorias unit seeks debt moratorium.
newsitem.headline: Victorias unit seeks debt moratorium.

text.p: Cash-strapped Victorias Milling Corp said on Monday its trading arm had asked the Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to shield it from its creditors.
North Negros Marketing Corp, which is 51-percent owned by Victorias, filed a petition for suspension of payments with the SEC, Victorias said in a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange.
"The forum for this legal action is confined within North Negros and its creditor banks and does not include Victorias," the sugar miller said.
State-controlled Land Bank of the Philippines said on Friday it had foreclosed some properties of North Negros in partial payments of its debts worth 465.62 million pesos.
Victorias has separetely sought a debt moratorium on principal payment of its 4.423 billion loans from 32 local and foreign creditors due to the slump in the local sugar industry.
It said it presented to its creditors a rehabilitation plan on Friday.

But some bank creditors of Victorias were thinking of foreclosure action after a meeting with Victorias officers failed to iron out details of a rehabilitation plan, a spokesman for the creditors said.
"(They) are not too happy with the lack of specifics," Isidro Alcantara, executive vice-president of Philippine Commercial and International Bank (PCIB), told reporters on Sunday.
Alcantara, the spokesman for the creditor banks, said banks which had extended secured loans to Victorias were "thinking of foreclosure because no serious recovery plan has been presented."
While debt restructuring efforts are still going on, some banks are "running out of time and patience," he added.
